newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan oil firms to rent Conoco LPG tank in Dubai.
newsitem.headline: Japan oil firms to rent Conoco LPG tank in Dubai.

text.p: Idemitsu Kosan Co Ltd said on Friday it and three other Japanese firms are planning to rent part of a liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) storage tank in Dubai from Conoco of the United States beginning around 1999.
This will be the first time that Japanese oil firms will use overseas storage facilities of substantial size, an Idemitsu spokesman said.
Idemitsu, Nippon Petroleum Gas Co Ltd, Showa Shell Sekiyu KK and Iwatani International Corp are expected to reach an agreement with Conoco on lease conditions as early as this autumn, he said.

The storage tank will enable the Japanese firms to buy relatively cheap LPG supplies in the summer from Middle Eastern countries and ship them to Japan in the winter, when global LPG demand and prices peak, a Showa Shell spokesman said.

Conoco, a unit of U.S.-based DuPont Co, is expected to complete construction of the 840,000-tonne underground salt cavern storage unit in 1999. About half of the storage capacity will be leased to the four Japanese firms, the Idemitsu spokesman said.
Annual storage fees will be around $30 per tonne, he added.
Nippon Petroleum Gas is a wholly owned subsidiary of Nippon Oil Co Ltd and Showa Shell is owned 50 percent by the Royal Dutch/Shell Group.
